deep.reconstruction:
Context: this folio is a working draft for Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). It sits in the part that classifies functions on the dissected surface T' by their discontinuities and then shows that two such functions are algebraically related. The previous page builds the integrals of the first kind w_1..w_p and the logarithmic integrals Π. It also gets the functions t that are infinite of order n at one point ε by differentiating with respect to the position z_ν of ε. The next page states the general existence problem via the Dirichlet principle, with prescribed local expansions a_ν log t + b_ν t^{-1} + c_ν t^{-2} + ... and jumps 2πi a_ν across cut lines l_ν.

(A) Top block (struck through and boxed in pencil). Readable gist: 'Wird nun die Function in einem Punkte der Fläche T unendlich, so kann sie, wenn man durch t eine Function bezeichnet, die in diesem Punkte unendlich klein von der ersten Ordnung wird, statt durch ... durch einen endlichen Ausdruck von der Form A log t + B t^{-1} + C t^{-2} + ... in eine stetige verwandelt werden.'
- Modern form: let P be a point of T and t a local uniformizing parameter vanishing to first order at P. Then t = z - z_P at an ordinary point, t = (z - z_P)^{1/m} at a branch point of order m-1, and t = (1/z)^{1/m} at infinity.
- An admissible singularity of f at P means that f - (A log t + B t^{-1} + C t^{-2} + ... + K t^{-k}) is continuous (indeed holomorphic) near P.
- This is the general principal part 'log term + finite Laurent tail', expressed in the local parameter rather than in z.
- The deleted earlier wording appears to say the same thing directly in terms of the order of infinity.

(B) Middle lines (struck/boxed), fragmentary.
- Line 1: 'Eine Function, die für einen Punkt der Fläche T unendlich ... unendlich von der ersten Ordnung wird.' This announces the case of a function with a single simple pole.
- Line 2: '... über die Existenzbedingungen (?) einer Function in T ergiebt'. This announces that the general construction yields the conditions for the existence of such functions; that is the Riemann-Roch-type count of the published §5.
- An isolated heading follows, possibly 'Fünfte/Ganze(?) Function', unreadable.

(C) Bottom paragraph. This is the main content, an essentially final version of the published text: 'Ist s eine Function von z, die in T n mal unendlich von der ersten Ordnung und sonst allenthalben stetig ist, und z' eine solche Function, die m mal unendlich von der ersten Ordnung ist, so entsprechen jedem Werthe von z n Punkte der Fläche T und also n Werthe von z' ... (wenn diese Werthe allgemein zu reden sämmtlich von einander verschieden sind) z' eine n-werthige Function von z und ebenso z eine m-werthige Function von z'.'
- Modern form: let X be a compact Riemann surface and f, g meromorphic on X of degrees n and m, i.e. with n and m simple poles counted with multiplicity.
- Step 1. f takes every value exactly n times (counted with multiplicity), by the argument principle.
- Step 2. For generic c, the fibre f^{-1}(c) consists of n distinct points.
- Step 3. The values of g on that fibre give n values. Hence g is an n-valued function of f; symmetrically, f is an m-valued function of g.
- Implicit next step (mine; it is drawn in the published §5). The elementary symmetric functions of these n values are single-valued and have only polar singularities as functions of f, hence are rational in f. So F(f, g) = 0 with F of degree n in g and of degree m in f. This is the passage from transcendentally defined functions to the algebraic curve.
errors: No mathematical errors in the legible text.
Step 2 is properly a genericity condition: values can coincide over branch points, or for special g. Riemann explicitly hedges this with 'allgemein zu reden'.
The draft does not argue why the symmetric functions are rational. That argument appears in the printed version.

results.what: Local normal form of admissible singularities: f minus (A log t + B/t + C/t^2 + ...) is continuous, with t a local parameter vanishing to first order (t=(z-z0)^{1/m} at branch points, (1/z)^{1/m} at infinity).
results.modern_name: principal parts in a local uniformizer; meromorphic/logarithmic singularities on a Riemann surface

results.what: Two meromorphic functions with n and m poles on a compact Riemann surface: each is an n- (resp. m-)valued function of the other, so they satisfy an algebraic equation of bidegree (m,n).
results.modern_name: every pair of meromorphic functions on a compact Riemann surface is algebraically dependent; degree of a meromorphic function = degree of the field extension C(X)/C(f)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (§5 of Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen)

results.what: Announcement of single-simple-pole functions and the existence conditions for them.
results.modern_name: Riemann (–Roch) count of functions with prescribed poles

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of passages that appear almost verbatim in Riemann's published 1857 Abelian functions paper (principal parts in a local parameter; n-valued/m-valued correspondence between functions). It is interesting only as evidence of how the text evolved.

checkable.asserts: On the elliptic curve, x has 2 poles (counted) and y has 3. Hence y is a 2-valued function of x and x a 3-valued function of y: F is of degree 2 in y and 3 in x.
Subtracting the expression A log t + B t^-1 + C t^-2 leaves a function continuous at t=0.
At a branch point of order m-1, t=(z-z0)^{1/m} is a local parameter vanishing to first order (here for t>0).
Hyperelliptic genus-2 example: x has degree 2 and y has degree 5, so the relation has bidegree (5 in x, 2 in y).

(wenn diese Werthe allgemein zu reden sämmtlich von einander verschieden sind) z' eine n-werthige Function von z und ebenso z eine m-werthige Function von z'.'
The machine's final clause 'z eine ...werthige Function von z' should be 'z eine m-werthige Function von z''; the earlier 'n Werthe von z'' was dropped.
